::: {#sol-count-pairs}

A pair can start with any of the 10 digits and end with any of the other 9,
and that counts each pair twice, once in each order:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{number of pairs}
&= \frac{10 \times 9}{2}
&& \text{(first digit, second digit, divided by the 2 orders of a pair)} \\
&= \frac{90}{2}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 45
&& \text{(divide)}
\end{aligned}
$$

That is 45 [features](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/course-overview.html#def-feature) to design and test by hand,
and @sol-three-or-eight shows that some pairs need more than one.

:::
